goal: Decide which de-identification technique the community collector applies to each field of a record before the record is published in the observation corpus.

app.name: uor-deidentification
app.title: Observation de-identification policy
app.purpose: Publish a collected field only as GDPR Article 4(5) pseudonymised data: suppress content, replace every identifier a platform shows only to its members with a keyed cryptographic hash (the ISO/IEC 20889 pseudonymization technique with a keyed hash, HMAC per FIPS 198-1) whose key is held apart from the corpus, and refuse to publish such an identifier when the key is missing.

fields.name: role
fields.means: the field's ISO/IEC 20889 attribute class: a direct identifier (it names a person or resolves to one, such as a user id, a message id or a thread id), a quasi-identifier (a time or a place a person acted), content the person wrote or named, or structure that names no person

fields.name: origin
fields.means: where the subject published the value: only to the members of a platform (a Discord guild), or in a world-readable source the corpus cites (git commit metadata, a GitHub account)

fields.name: key
fields.means: whether the collection run holds the secret pseudonymisation key

meanings.pseudonymize: publish the keyed hash of the value, never the value
meanings.retain: publish the value as the source holds it
meanings.indeterminate: no keyed hash can be made, so the record is not published

rules.why: GDPR Article 5(1)(c) data minimisation and the ISO/IEC 20889 suppression technique: CHAOSS Chat Platform Inclusivity counts messages and participants, never their text or names

ENISA Pseudonymisation techniques and best practices (2019), Cryptographic hash function: an unkeyed hash of an identifier is reversed by hashing the identifier space, so it is not pseudonymisation under GDPR Article 4(5)

GDPR Article 4(5) and ENISA (2019), Message Authentication Code, and the ISO/IEC 20889 pseudonymization technique: a keyed hash (HMAC-SHA-256, FIPS 198-1) whose key is kept separately and never published
LINDDUN Linking and Identifying: the subject published the identifier in the world-readable source the corpus cites, so its digest links nothing the source does not

app.otherwiseWhy: ISO/IEC 20889 attribute classes: quasi-identifiers the measurement needs and structure that names no person are kept; the keyed pseudonym breaks their linkage to outside data

properties.why: an identifier a platform shows only to its members is never published as it is
no pseudonym is made without the key

stakeholders.name: Discord member
stakeholders.text: Talks in the Foundation's Discord and needs no one outside the guild, and no one inside it, to turn the published corpus back into their messages.

stakeholders.name: Community and Outreach Committee
stakeholders.text: Needs the CHAOSS chat metrics measured on the Foundation's live chat from a corpus anyone can replay.

stakeholders.name: Data protection reviewer
stakeholders.text: Needs every published field to be pseudonymised, suppressed or kept for a stated reason under GDPR Article 4(5) and ISO/IEC 20889.

components.name: Community collector
components.text: observations/collect.py, which asks this app for every field of observations/deidentification.json before it records or publishes anything.

components.name: Pseudonymisation key
components.text: The DISCORD_PSEUDONYM_KEY secret, held only by the collection run.

threats.name: Re-identification of published activity
threats.text: A member's id or a message id in the public corpus is looked up in Discord or hashed, and the member's activity is linked back to them.

control.name: Keyed pseudonyms only
control.text: A restricted direct identifier is never retained, and without the key it is never published.

threats.name: Timing linkage inside the guild
threats.text: A member who reads a channel matches a pseudonymised message's time and channel to the message they saw.
threats.accepted: The member already sees the message and its author in Discord; the time and channel are what the measurement needs, and the keyed pseudonym keeps the match from extending to the member's other activity outside what they can see.
